subject.title: fix: tighten control ui input validation [AI]

question: Should config merge patches globally reject the four legacy accessor-method names, or preserve them in schema-owned arbitrary-key maps?
rationale: Ordinary writes to these names do not mutate prototypes, so the broader rejection is defense-in-depth with a real but uncommon compatibility cost that requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Preserve map-key compatibility
options.body: Scope the rejection to object positions where these names are not legitimate data, while adding allowances and tests for schema-owned arbitrary-key maps.

options.title: Accept global rejection
options.body: Keep the global merge-patch filter and explicitly accept, document, and test that these four previously valid names are dropped at every path.

recommendation.title: Preserve map-key compatibility
recommendation.body: Scope the rejection to object positions where these names are not legitimate data, while adding allowances and tests for schema-owned arbitrary-key maps.

likelyOwner.reason: The current merge-patch guard and settings-path history most strongly route this contract decision to steipete.
